subject: What to do after updating shiny on Spark?

messages.author: c5790e857463cacd
messages.subject: What to do after updating shiny on Spark?
parts:
Hello,
 I have a shiny application on spark (here: spark.rstudio.com/johnpaul/Water ). Recently I decide to change the table that appears on the raw data tab from a datatable using the new renderDataTable() command. This worked great on my desktop, but when I uploaded to spark it did not recognize the renderDataTable commands. I realized that I had not updated shiny to 0.80 from 0.70 on spark. After some flailing around (I don't use Linux regularly) I got this done. However, the application still would not work with the DataTable, so I put back the older table style. My assumption was that the application was still using the 0.70 version of shiny.

So, is there anything I need to do to restart my application so that it uses shiny 0.80.  I am pretty confident that most of the time no one is looking at it,- so will it stop and restart on its own?  If I need to do something to restart the application I would be using the terminal command line rather than RStudio, as I only recently started using RStudio.

Thanks for any help,

John Paul

messages.author: 3da48b33a2f506a9
messages.subject: Re: What to do after updating shiny on Spark?
parts:
John,

I noticed that a new process was started for your application a few hours ago, so it seems that you were able to do this. But for reference, you can create an empty file called "restart.txt" in your application directory on spark, or use "touch" command to change the timestamp on it; this will force s restart of your application.

Fereshteh
